compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The bounded Agent operation [rebar:kingsize-unfair-blackbird] changes two observable compatibility seams by design: successful retries now expose whole-run usage, and Pydantic wraps retry exhaustion in broad `UnexpectedModelBehavior`. Rebar consumers require one truthful operation row, typed resolution behavior, consumed-so-far diagnostics, and complete final-failure artifacts (`src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:362-381`, `src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py:48-157`, `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:491-642`).

## Approach
Treat the Pydantic Agent run as the accounting unit. Project its aggregate `RunUsage` once through `_extract_usage`, `agent_call`, gate aggregates, and the durable JSONL row; never subtract rejected output attempts or emit per-attempt rows. On exhaustion, walk only the standard Python cause chain and re-raise the exact Rebar-owned `StructuredOutputError` object found there, retaining the `UnretryableOutputError` subtype for repeated output-size failure. Leave unrelated `UnexpectedModelBehavior` unchanged. Capture the complete final provider response only at terminal failure through the existing opt-in artifact policy; retry-wire omission never mutates stored messages.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py` — whole-run usage extraction and compatibility result.
- `src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py`, `src/rebar/llm/failure.py` — exact cause-chain restoration and sanitized consumed counters.
- `src/rebar/llm/agent_call.py`, `src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py` — one-row success/failure recording and complete final artifact timing.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — verify existing aggregates retain the complete operation counters without a parallel attempt field.
- Focused usage, failure-matrix, hardening, artifact, and plan-review tests.

## Testing
- Successful invalid-then-valid output with attempt usage 5 and 7 reports requests=2 and output_tokens=12 in memory, aggregate telemetry, and one JSONL row.
- Validation and output-size exhaustion restore their exact Rebar objects; an unrelated upstream exception remains untouched.
- Terminal failure preserves consumed requests/tokens and stores only the complete final response when artifact capture is enabled.
- Historical rows and pricing remain compatible because no new core usage field is introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A successful two-attempt Agent run reports the sum of both attempts in `_usage`, Pass-1 aggregate telemetry, and exactly one durable JSONL row; verified by focused usage and plan-review tests.
- [ ] Validation exhaustion re-raises the identical Rebar `StructuredOutputError`, repeated output-size exhaustion re-raises its identical `UnretryableOutputError`, and unrelated `UnexpectedModelBehavior` remains untranslated; verified by identity and negative-guard tests.
- [ ] Failure diagnostics retain consumed requests, tool calls, and provider-reported tokens without creating a fictional usage value for a call that reported none; verified by the failure-matrix suite.
- [ ] When parse-failure artifacts are enabled, only terminal failure writes an artifact and that artifact contains the complete final provider response even when the retry wire omitted an earlier response; verified by artifact-content and file-count tests.
- [ ] Existing pricing and usage reports remain byte-compatible apart from the approved higher counters after successful retry; verified by historical-row and pricing fixtures.
- [ ] `_usage` and usage JSONL contain no `candidate_requests` or other competing request-budget field; verified by schema assertions.
